outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no accepted proof of Szpiro's conjecture as stated has appeared; the in-window events are an unconditional bound for all elliptic curves over Q that is exponential in the conductor and so does not settle the statement (Pasten, arXiv 2609.17390, 15 Sep 2026), a partial Frey-height bound for integral j-invariant (Pasten, arXiv 2608.23559, 24 Aug 2026), a 2024 claimed proof of abc and of the arithmetic Szpiro inequality via Mochizuki's IUT that remains unaccepted (Joshi, arXiv 2403.10430, 15 Mar 2024), a conditional abelian-variety result (Gao and Gu, arXiv 2608.22285, Aug 2026), and statistical or family results; the one restricted-class proof of the statement as written (Pasten, arXiv 2308.07114) was first posted in August 2023 and published in CUBO on 31 May 2026.
problem_asks: (1) For every ε > 0, a constant C(ε) depending only on ε and not on the curve. (2) For every elliptic curve E defined over Q, with minimal discriminant Δ and conductor f: |Δ| ≤ C(ε)·f^(6+ε). Unpacked: (a) the quantity bounded is |Δ| itself, not log|Δ|; (b) the exponent is the fixed value 6+ε, polynomial in f; (c) the claim ranges over all E/Q, with no exceptional set; (d) it does not claim sharpness of the exponent. The n-conjecture parent is not part of this record.

events.what_happened: Shinichi Mochizuki posted his four inter-universal Teichmüller theory papers (IUT I to IV) on his own RIMS web page in late August 2012, with no arXiv posting and no announcement. He presented them as a proof of the abc conjecture, and Wikipedia reports that he claimed a proof of Szpiro's conjecture by developing IUT. The day is not settled across sources (30 or 31 August), so only the month is recorded. The papers were later published in Publ. RIMS (secondary sources give 2021; not verified against the journal). This is the one route the search found to the full statement for all E/Q.
events.revisions: Posted on the author's RIMS web page late August 2012 (30 or 31 August per different sources). Publ. RIMS 2021 per secondary sources (not opened). Kodai Math. J. 2022 write-up of effective versions over number fields is recorded as a separate event (fesenko-2020-iut-explicit).
events.delivers: As reported by Wikipedia, a proof of Szpiro's conjecture as stated, for all E/Q, obtained through IUT. Mochizuki's abc claim implies the statement in its modified form, which is equivalent to abc. The claim is for the full statement, not a restricted case.
events.remains: Nothing, if the claim is accepted. The claim is disputed (see checked_by and doubts). Under the record's own reading of the disputed step, the statement is not established.

checked_by.qualification: Research mathematicians; visited RIMS in March 2018 to work through the proof with Mochizuki and Yuichiro Hoshi, per secondary reports.
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote a critique (Why abc is still a conjecture, first issued May 2018, updated Sept 2018) identifying a gap at Corollary 3.12 of IUT III. Wikipedia quotes their conclusion that the issues are so severe that small modifications will not rescue the proof strategy. Mochizuki disputes the characterisation and replied in 2018. The critique's PDF was not readable through the fetch tool, so the quotation is second-hand.

events.doubts: (1) Scholze and Stix identify a specific gap at Corollary 3.12 and Mochizuki denies it; per Wikipedia the papers 'have not been accepted by the mathematical community as providing a proof of the conjecture'. (2) Dimitrov's 2012 commentary, as quoted by the nLab (search snippet only), says nothing like Theorem 1.10 of IUT IV could hold as written. (3) Conrad's 2015 notes (search snippet only) say the method as formulated does not yield explicit constants, so it cannot give an effective proof. (4) The LANA project's July 2026 interim report says some points in the deduction of Corollary 3.12 from Theorem 3.11 remain unclear; it reaches no verdict (see lana-2026-iut-formalisation). (5) Joshi's 2024 to 2025 preprints defend the proof; Mochizuki's March 2024 report, as Woit describes it, rejects them as containing no meaningful mathematics (see joshi-2024-iii and joshi-2024-iv).
events.direction: Claims a proof of the statement (affirmative direction), via the IUT route to abc and the modified Szpiro form.

events.what_happened: M. Ram Murty and Hector Pasten, 'Modular forms and effective Diophantine approximation', J. Number Theory 133 (2013), no. 11, pp. 3739 to 3754 (per the reference list of arXiv 2609.17390; the paper itself was not opened). Pasten's 2026 preprint says that the best unconditional bound for all E/Q, log Δ ≪ N log N with an absolute implied constant, dates from this 2013 work with Murty.
events.delivers: An effective unconditional bound for all E/Q of the form log|Δ| ≪ N log N, with an absolute constant, where N is the conductor. The exponent is only a linear power of N inside the logarithm, so the bound is exponential in the conductor. It does not give the statement, which asks for a polynomial bound on |Δ| itself.
events.remains: The polynomial bound |Δ| ≤ C(ε)·f^(6+ε) for all E/Q.
events.direction: Consistent with the statement; a weaker bound on the same quantity.

events.what_happened: Hector Pasten, 'Shimura curves and the abc conjecture', arXiv 1705.09251, v1 25 May 2017, last revised v4 5 July 2018. Published as J. Number Theory 254 (2024), pp. 214 to 335 (per the 2026 preprint's reference list). The abstract says the paper develops a framework for studying Szpiro's and abc conjectures by means of Shimura curves and their maps to elliptic curves. Its applications are improved effective bounds for the Faltings height of elliptic curves over Q in terms of the conductor, polynomial bounds on discriminant valuations, and a modular approach to Szpiro's conjecture over totally real number fields.
events.revisions: v1 25 May 2017; v2 4 June 2017; v3 27 Aug 2017; v4 5 July 2018. Journal version J. Number Theory 254 (2024) per the 2026 reference list.
events.delivers: Partial results toward the statement: effective Faltings-height bounds in terms of the conductor, and polynomial-in-conductor bounds on products of p-adic valuations of Δ. It does not state a bound on |Δ| of the statement's form over Q, as far as the abstract shows.
events.remains: The statement over Q with exponent 6+ε.
events.direction: Partial results; consistent with the statement.

events.what_happened: Michael A. Bennett and Soroosh Yazdani, 'A local version of Szpiro's conjecture', Experimental Mathematics 21(2) (2012). A preprint PDF on Bennett's UBC page is dated February 2012 according to a search snippet. The PDF returned only its section headings through the fetch tool. The headings include 'Applications to Szpiro's Conjecture' and 'The local Szpiro conjecture: sharpness'. The restriction described here comes from the search summary of Pasten's 2023 introduction, not from the paper itself.
events.revisions: Preprint PDF dated February 2012 (search snippet); journal Experimental Mathematics 21(2), 2012.
events.delivers: Per the search summary, a local (per-prime) version of the statement under extra hypotheses: a large prime divides the conductor, and the curve has a nontrivial rational isogeny. Not a global statement over Q.
events.remains: The global statement for all E/Q, and all curves outside the stated hypotheses.
events.doubts: The hypotheses were not checked against the paper's text; the PDF was not readable.
events.direction: A restricted local case; consistent with the statement.

events.what_happened: Shinichi Mochizuki, Ivan Fesenko, Yuichiro Hoshi, Arata Minamide and Wojciech Porowski, 'Explicit estimates in inter-universal Teichmüller theory', Kyoto RIMS preprint (November 2020 according to a search snippet), published Kodai Mathematical Journal 45(2) (2022), pp. 175 to 236. Per the search abstract, the paper gives numerically effective versions of the non-effective Vojta, ABC and Szpiro statements over number fields that Mochizuki had established within IUT, together with effective ABC inequalities over Q and imaginary quadratic fields. The Kodai abstract page returned empty and the author PDF was not readable, so this is from the search snippet only.
events.revisions: RIMS preprint November 2020 (search snippet); Kodai Math. J. 45(2), 2022.
events.delivers: Per the search snippet, effective Szpiro-type statements over number fields, derived from the IUT framework. Whether it covers the Q case of the statement with the polynomial exponent is not established from what was read.
events.remains: The effective polynomial statement over Q for all E is not shown to be established by this paper, as far as the snippets show.
events.doubts: Depends on IUT, which is disputed (see mochizuki-2012-iut). The paper was not read.
events.direction: Effective Szpiro-type results over number fields, conditional on the IUT framework.

events.what_happened: Rafael von Känel, 'On Szpiro's Discriminant Conjecture', arXiv 1310.7980 (October 2013 by arXiv identifier). Not opened; the search snippet says it gives effective, exponential versions of Szpiro-type discriminant bounds for curves over number fields, including genus one and two curves.
events.delivers: Per the search snippet, an analogue over number fields, with exponential rather than polynomial bounds. Not the statement over Q.
events.remains: The statement over Q with its polynomial exponent.
events.direction: An analogue over number fields; consistent with the statement.

events.what_happened: Proofs of the geometric (function-field) Szpiro inequality, by Kim (1997), Amorós et al. (2000), Zhang (2001) and Beauville (2002), according to a search summary of Pasten's 2023 introduction and a search result on Bogomolov's proof. These are not opened. The first is dated only to 1997; the record uses the first year.
events.delivers: Settles the geometric analogue over function fields, not the arithmetic statement over Q. It is listed because the question is an analogue, not because it resolves the statement.
events.remains: The arithmetic statement over Q.
events.direction: Analogue in a different setting (function fields, geometric); consistent with the statement.

events.what_happened: Mestre and Oesterlé proved Szpiro's conjecture for elliptic curves whose minimal discriminant is a prime power, per Pasten's 2023 introduction and a search summary. Their paper was not located and the date is not established from the sources read.
events.delivers: The statement for the restricted class of E/Q whose minimal discriminant is a prime power.
events.remains: All other E/Q.
events.doubts: The exact theorem and hypotheses were not checked against the original paper.
events.direction: A restricted case of the statement; consistent with it.

events.what_happened: Pesenti and Szpiro proved Szpiro's conjecture for elliptic curves with integral j-invariant, per Pasten's 2023 introduction and a search summary. The paper was not located and the date is not established from the sources read.
events.delivers: The statement for the restricted class of E/Q with integral j-invariant.
events.remains: All E/Q with non-integral j-invariant.
events.doubts: Not checked against the original paper.
events.direction: A restricted case of the statement; consistent with it.

events.what_happened: Kirti Joshi, 'Construction of Arithmetic Teichmüller Spaces III: A Rosetta Stone and a proof of Mochizuki's Corollary 3.12', arXiv 2401.13508, v1 24 Jan 2024, two days before the freeze. Later versions: v2 15 Mar 2024, v3 27 Jun 2024, v4 24 Feb 2025 (current). The abstract, read directly, says the paper establishes 'a proof Mochizuki's Corollary 3.12' and offers a Rosetta Stone for reading IUT alongside the author's theory. The body was not read.
events.revisions: v1 24 Jan 2024; v2 15 Mar 2024; v3 27 Jun 2024; v4 24 Feb 2025 (current).
events.delivers: Per the abstract, a proof of Corollary 3.12 of IUT III, the step the Scholze and Stix critique targets. This is one step of the IUT route to abc and to the statement. It does not, on its own, prove the statement.
events.remains: The rest of the IUT deduction from Corollary 3.12 to abc and to the statement, and the statement itself.
events.doubts: The claim is the author's alone. Per Woit's March 2024 post, Mochizuki's report calls the author profoundly ignorant of IUT and the series without meaningful mathematical content; Woit knows of no one who has gone through the argument in detail. The Lean project's July 2026 interim report reaches no verdict on Corollary 3.12 (see lana-2026-iut-formalisation). This is a party to the dispute, so it is a signal, not a verification.
events.direction: Claims to prove Corollary 3.12 (affirmative, for one step of the IUT route to the statement).

events.what_happened: Hector Pasten, 'Szpiro's conjecture when the denominator of the j-invariant is small', arXiv 2308.07114, v1 14 Aug 2023, v2 15 Aug 2023 ('References updated'). Published as CUBO, A Mathematical Journal 28(2) (2026), pp. 383 to 389, on 31 May 2026 (DOI 10.56754/0719-0646.2802.383). The first public written argument is the 2023 arXiv posting, so the event is dated to it. The abstract says the paper proves Szpiro's conjecture for elliptic curves over the rationals whose j-invariant has a denominator of logarithmic size with respect to its numerator.
events.revisions: v1 14 Aug 2023; v2 15 Aug 2023 ('References updated'); CUBO 28(2) published 31 May 2026.
events.delivers: Theorem 1.2 (arXiv HTML v2, read through a model-mediated summary): for fixed A, B > 0 and every E/Q with den(j) ≤ A·(log num(j))^B, |Δ_E| ≤ A·16^(B+1)·N_E^(B+5)·(log N_E)^B. Corollary 1.3 specialises to B = 1: den(j) ≤ A·log num(j) gives |Δ| ≤ 256A·N^6·log N, which has the statement's form with exponent 6+ε. The paper's own statement is therefore for the class of E/Q whose j-invariant denominator is logarithmic in its numerator; for B > 1 the exponent exceeds 6. Restricted to that class, the statement is proved.
events.remains: Every E/Q whose j-invariant denominator is not logarithmic in its numerator, which is the general statement over Q.

checked_by.who: Editors and referees of CUBO, A Mathematical Journal (Universidad de La Frontera)
checked_by.qualification: Peer-reviewed mathematics journal; referee identities and reports are not visible on the pages read.
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, 31 May 2026. No referee report is public.

events.time_since_posted: about 26 months since the arXiv posting (Aug 2023); about 4.5 months since CUBO publication (31 May 2026)
events.doubts: No specific doubt about the restricted-case proof was found. The 2023 introduction says the strongest unconditional result valid for all E/Q is log Δ ≤ (1/4+ε)·N log N + O_ε(1), attributed to the author and improving Murty and Pasten. This is consistent at the level of order of magnitude with the 2026 preprint's 'N log N, dating to 2013'; the 2023 constant is sharper.
events.direction: Proves the statement's inequality for the restricted class named: a case of the statement, not an analogue.

events.what_happened: Kirti Joshi, 'Construction of Arithmetic Teichmüller Spaces IV: Proof of the abc-conjecture', arXiv 2403.10430, v1 15 Mar 2024, v2 24 Feb 2025 (current; 'expanded and revised edition of my March 2024 submission'). The v2 abstract says the theory leads, using Mochizuki's rubric, 'to a proof of the abc-conjecture (as asserted by Mochizuki)'. The body states Conjecture 2.2.1, the arithmetic Szpiro conjecture for elliptic curves over Q, as a conjecture, and Theorem 2.10.1 lists among its consequences an 'Arithmetic Szpiro Inequality' for elliptic curves over number fields, which includes Q. The HTML was read in summarised chunks and Theorem 7.1.1 and the acknowledgements were not seen in full.
events.revisions: v1 15 Mar 2024; v2 24 Feb 2025 (current). Per a search snippet, the v1 abstract stated the abc claim more directly.
events.delivers: Claims the abc conjecture, and within it the arithmetic Szpiro inequality over number fields, including Q (Theorem 2.10.1 consequence (2), as read). It does not claim the statement directly, but the modified Szpiro form is equivalent to abc, so an accepted abc proof would bring the statement with it. Whether Q is covered by the derivation is not confirmed from the visible text.
events.remains: Everything, unless the IUT chain is accepted; no independent verification exists in the sources read.

checked_by.who: Peter Scholze, as reported second-hand by Peter Woit
checked_by.qualification: Scholze co-wrote the 2018 critique of IUT; Woit is a mathematician who blogs about the dispute. The report is second-hand.
checked_by.what_they_did: Per Woit (25 Mar 2024), Scholze posted a MathOverflow comment indicating where Joshi's attempt runs into trouble, and Scholze and other experts are so far unconvinced. The MathOverflow thread was not opened.

events.time_since_posted: about 31 months since v1 (15 Mar 2024); about 20 months since v2 (24 Feb 2025)
events.doubts: (1) Mochizuki's March 2024 report, as Woit describes it, calls the preprints profoundly ignorant of IUT and without meaningful mathematical content. This is a party to the dispute: a signal, not a verdict. (2) Scholze's MathOverflow objection, reported second-hand; the thread was not read. (3) The author's own later reports and letter (joshi-2025-final-report, joshi-2025-nov-letter-faq) are described as partly conflicting, and were read only second-hand. (4) Woit knows of no one who has gone through the argument in detail.
events.direction: Asserts that abc holds, and with it the arithmetic Szpiro inequality over number fields, including Q; affirmative.

events.what_happened: Stephanie Chan, 'Almost all elliptic curves with prescribed torsion have Szpiro ratio close to the expected value', arXiv 2407.13850, submitted 18 July 2024 (math.NT), single version. It shows that for E/Q with a fixed torsion subgroup, ordered by naive height, almost all curves have Szpiro ratio arbitrarily close to the expected value, and gives bounds for the ratio for almost all curves in certain one-parameter families.
events.delivers: A statement about almost all E/Q with a fixed torsion subgroup: the Szpiro ratio log|Δ|/log f is close to its expected value. It is a statement about almost all curves, not every curve, and gives no bound of the statement's form for any individual curve.
events.remains: Every individual curve. The statement is not implied by an almost-all result.
events.direction: Statistical; neither confirms nor refutes the statement, and is consistent with it.

events.what_happened: José Cuevas Barrientos and Hector Pasten, 'On the greatest prime factor of polynomial values and subexponential Szpiro in families', arXiv 2504.15971, v1 22 Apr 2025, v2 4 Aug 2025, v3 7 Sep 2025 ('Fixed some references'). The paper combines a modular approach to abc with the linear-forms-in-logarithms method to prove unconditional bounds for Szpiro's problem in one-parameter families.
events.revisions: v1 22 Apr 2025; v2 4 Aug 2025; v3 7 Sep 2025 (current).
events.delivers: Theorem 1.1: for the elliptic surface y² = x³ + A(t)x + B(t), with A, B in Z[t] coprime over Q and nonzero discriminant of the family, log|Δ_n| ≪ h(E_n) ≤ exp(κ·sqrt((log N_n)·log*_2 N_n)) for all integers n outside a finite exceptional set. Corollary 1.2: log|Δ_n| ≪_ε N_n^ε for every ε > 0. The bound is for log|Δ_n| and is subexponential in log N_n, but not polynomial in N_n. It covers a family, not all E/Q.
events.remains: The statement over all E/Q; for the family case, the polynomial-in-conductor bound on |Δ|.
events.direction: Consistent with the statement; a family analogue with a bound far weaker than the polynomial exponent.

events.what_happened: Ziyang Gao and Kaiyuan Gu, 'Uniformity in rational torsion and small points on abelian varieties', arXiv 2608.22285, v1 23 Aug 2026 (submitted by Gao), v2 31 Aug 2026. The abstract says the method is inspired by Vojta's proof of the Mordell conjecture. For number fields, both the Uniform Boundedness and Lang–Silverman conjectures are proved under a high-dimensional Szpiro conjecture the authors propose, which they say is weaker than Hindry's generalised Szpiro conjecture (Conjecture 3.4 of Hindry). Wikipedia's torsion page describes this as a proof assuming a generalised Szpiro conjecture.
events.revisions: v1 23 Aug 2026; v2 31 Aug 2026 (adds supercurrents to Section 5.2, rewrites Section 5.3's proof, corrects typos).
events.delivers: Conditional results for abelian varieties over number fields, under a high-dimensional Szpiro conjecture the authors propose, plus unconditional explicit bounds for some function-field cases. Nothing unconditional about the statement for elliptic curves over Q.
events.remains: The statement itself, which is not addressed. The conditional hypothesis is a generalisation of the statement, not the statement.
events.direction: Conditional on a generalised Szpiro conjecture, for abelian varieties; does not bear on the statement's proof status.

events.what_happened: Kirti Joshi, 'Final Report on the Mochizuki-Scholze-Stix Controversy', arXiv 2505.10568, submitted 29 April 2025 (single version). The abstract reads: 'This report provides my mathematical findings regarding the Mochizuki-Scholze-Stix controversy surrounding Mochizuki's Inter-Universal Teichmüller Theory.' The abstract page does not mention Szpiro or abc. The PDF was not readable through the fetch tool.
events.delivers: The abstract states no result for the statement. Second-hand descriptions only: judgments on the Scholze and Stix objection and on the status of abc, conditional on Joshi's additions. Content not verified.
events.remains: Not established from what was read.
events.doubts: The author is a party to the dispute. Mochizuki responded to Joshi's earlier material in March 2024 (per Woit); no response to this report was read.
events.direction: No direction stated in the abstract; second-hand descriptions say it asserts the Scholze and Stix objections fail.

events.what_happened: Kirti Joshi, a letter to Peter Woit dated 1 November 2025 and an 'FAQ about the proof of the abc-conjecture', described in search snippets as defending the abc proof, and arguing that the concept of a 'universe' or '∈-loop' does not occur in the Scholze and Stix (2018) critique. Neither document was opened; the FAQ's arXiv posting is reported on hold.
events.delivers: A rebuttal and FAQ defending the abc claim. No new theorem about the statement is reported in the snippets.
events.remains: Everything, as far as the snippets show.
events.doubts: The author's own reply in the dispute. Read only from snippets.
events.direction: Asserts the abc claim stands; affirmative; no direction on the statement beyond that.

events.what_happened: Lemuel Schaine Harris, 'Proof of the ABC Conjecture Finiteness via the Subspace Theorem and Explicit Height Bounds', a Zenodo preprint published 27 July 2025 (version v1). It claims a complete proof of abc finiteness via the Subspace Theorem.
events.delivers: Claims an abc result, which is a different question from the statement. The claim is not assessed here.
events.remains: Not assessed.
events.doubts: Self-published on Zenodo; no reviewer or endorsement statement on the page. The record page was read, but not the mathematics.
events.direction: Claims an abc result (affirmative); not assessed and not about the statement as written.

events.what_happened: Christopher Pompetzki, 'ABC Conjecture Done Right: The Axlerian Annihilation of Analysis...', a Zenodo preprint published 8 March 2026 (v1). The abstract says a chain of statements is established toward the ABC conjecture and that 'The ABC Conjecture follows.'
events.delivers: Claims abc; the record does not explain how the chain of statements reaches the claim. Not about the statement as written.
events.remains: Not assessed.
events.doubts: The page offers no evidence of peer review, and its abstract includes non-serious text. The proof sketch identifies one quantity with another and cites a bound without showing how it applies, per the fetch summary.
events.direction: Claims abc (affirmative); not assessed.

events.what_happened: Project LANA ('Lean for ANAbelian geometry', ZEN Mathematics Center, led by Fumiharu Kato) published its 'Project LANA Interim Report on IUT Theory' and held a meeting on 17 July 2026. The report says there are points that remain unclear in deriving Corollary 3.12 of IUT III from Theorem 3.11, and that it has not reconstructed a proof of the required compatibility. Kato: 'At this stage, we have not been able to conclude whether the abc conjecture has been proven by IUT theory.' Mochizuki gave an April 2026 talk on preliminary progress toward formalising IUT in Lean (per secondary sources; the progress-report PDF was not readable). The report PDF was not readable.
events.revisions: Interim report July 2026; Mochizuki formalisation talk April 2026 (secondary); project announced March 2026 (secondary).
events.delivers: No proof and no refutation. The interim status: a compatibility step that the IUT route needs is not reconstructed. It bears on the statement only through the IUT abc route.
events.remains: The whole statement; the project has reached no judgement on the IUT argument.

checked_by.who: Fumiharu Kato and the LANA Project (ZEN Mathematics Center)
checked_by.qualification: Project leader and formalisation team; qualifications beyond the project role not checked.
checked_by.what_they_did: Interim report, July 2026: identifies unclear points in the Theorem 3.11 to Corollary 3.12 step and withholds judgement on whether IUT proves abc.

events.time_since_posted: about 3 months since the July 2026 interim report

machine_checked.system: Lean (project LANA; Mochizuki's Lean code for 3.11.5 to 3.12 is skeletal per secondary reports)

events.doubts: The project reports points it does not yet understand. A secondary headline (zeli.app) says the step 'cannot be formalized'; the primary page says only that points remain unclear and that final judgement is reserved, so the headline overstates it. Not a verdict either way.
events.direction: No direction; an unfinished formalisation of the IUT chain that reports an unresolved step.

events.what_happened: Hector Pasten, 'Power-saving bounds for Thue–Mahler and Mordell equations', arXiv 2608.23559, v1 24 Aug 2026, v2 6 Sep 2026 (current). The abstract says the paper proves effective bounds for cubic Thue–Mahler equations, improves Stark's bound for Mordell's equation, and 'gives a power-saving improvement in the conductor aspect of the strongest currently available bounds for Frey's height conjecture (a strengthening of Szpiro's conjecture) in the case of elliptic curves over Q with integral j-invariant.' Theorem 1.6, read through a model-mediated fetch of the HTML: for all E/Q with integral j-invariant, h(E) ≪ N^(1/2)·(log N)^4, with an absolute effective constant. Conjecture 1.5 is the height conjecture h(E) ≤ c·log N for all E/Q. arXiv 2609.17390 cites this paper as the source of its N^(1/2+ε) bound for integral j.
events.delivers: For Frey's height conjecture (which the paper says strengthens Szpiro's conjecture), a partial bound for E/Q with integral j-invariant: h(E) ≪ N^(1/2)·(log N)^4 for the Faltings height. The paper's bound is on the Faltings height, not directly on |Δ|, so it does not give the statement, which is a bound on |Δ|. Restricted to integral j-invariant, and to a stronger conjecture than the statement.
events.remains: The statement for all E/Q; Frey's height conjecture for all E/Q; the non-integral-j case.
events.doubts: Single author, no reviewer on record. Only the HTML rendering of its Section 6 and the abstract were read; the full text was not checked character by character.
events.direction: Consistent with the statement; partial bound for a stronger conjecture in a restricted class.

events.what_happened: Hector Pasten, 'Improved bounds for Szpiro's conjecture', arXiv 2609.17390, submitted 15 September 2026 (single version, v1; math.NT; single author). The abstract says that the best known bound for all E/Q is log Δ ≪ N log N, dating to 2013; the paper proves log Δ ≪ N log log N, previously known only under GRH; for semistable curves it proves log Δ ≪ N. The methods build on the author's work on abc via Shimura curves. Section 1: Theorem 1.1 (for E/Q and an admissible factorisation N = DM with a prime ℓ not dividing N, h(E) ≪ M·φ(D)·log ℓ, with an absolute effective constant); Corollary 1.2 (h(E) ≪ N log log N for all E/Q); Corollary 1.3 (for E/Q semistable outside a finite set S, h(E) ≪_S N). The introduction also states Frey-type bounds: h(E) ≪ N^(1/3+ε) for Frey curves, and h(E) ≪ N^(1/2+ε) for integral j-invariant, citing the author's [7] (arXiv 2608.23559). It says Frey's height conjecture is stronger than Szpiro's, and that bound (1.1) shows the height conjecture implies Szpiro's conjecture.
events.revisions: v1 only (15 Sep 2026); no later version found by 13 Oct 2026.
events.delivers: Unconditional, for all E/Q, with an absolute effective constant: log|Δ| ≪ N log log N, and for semistable E: log|Δ| ≪ N. These move the bound on the statement's own quantity |Δ| in terms of the conductor f, from exp(N log N) to exp(N log log N) in shape. A bound exponential in the conductor does not imply the statement, which needs |Δ| ≤ C(ε)·f^(6+ε), i.e. log|Δ| ≤ (6+ε)·log f + O_ε(1). It gives no bound on the Szpiro ratio log|Δ|/log f. Also h(E) bounds as listed (Faltings height, Frey-type).
events.remains: The statement itself (the polynomial bound for all E/Q); the Szpiro-ratio bound; Frey's height conjecture (h(E) ≪ log N), which the statement follows from.

events.direction: Consistent with the statement. Improves the conductor-dependence of log|Δ| for all E/Q from N log N to N log log N, and to N for semistable E, but remains exponential in N; does not prove or refute the polynomial bound.

disputes.summary: Mochizuki's IUT claims a proof of abc and, per Wikipedia, of Szpiro's conjecture. Scholze and Stix (2018) identify a gap at Corollary 3.12 of IUT III. Joshi's 2024 to 2025 preprints (joshi-2024-iii, joshi-2024-iv) claim to prove Corollary 3.12 and abc; Mochizuki's March 2024 report, as Woit describes it, rejects them. The LANA project's July 2026 interim report identifies unclear points and reaches no verdict. Not resolved here.

The author's 2023 paper gives the unconditional bound log Δ ≤ (1/4+ε)·N log N + O_ε(1) as the strongest result for all E/Q; the 2026 preprint says the best known bound is log Δ ≪ N log N, dating to 2013. These agree at the level of order of magnitude; the 2023 paper gives a sharper constant. This is not a priority dispute and is not resolved here.

The same author's two 2026 AI statements name the same model family differently: arXiv 2608.23559 says 'Claude Fable 5', arXiv 2609.17390 says 'Claude Fable 5.1'. Both are recorded exactly as written; the later pass should not normalise them.

summary: Szpiro's conjecture as stated (|Δ| ≤ C(ε)·f^(6+ε) for all E/Q) appears open in every source I could read, and no counterexample has been proposed. The sources were arXiv abstract and HTML pages, the CUBO journal page, the Wikipedia article, the ZEN LANA page, the Pith AI-referee page, Woit's 2024 blog post, the OpenAI openai/math catalogue (scanned in six chunks), and search snippets for older items. The most important in-window event is Pasten's arXiv 2609.17390 (15 Sep 2026), which proves log|Δ| ≪ N log log N for all E/Q with an absolute effective constant, and log|Δ| ≪ N for semistable curves. Those bounds are exponential in the conductor and so give no bound on the Szpiro ratio log|Δ|/log f; by my reading they do not move the statement's form, though they do move the bound on the statement's own quantity. Its introduction ties Frey-type height bounds to the statement: Frey's height conjecture implies Szpiro's, and the paper's h(E) ≪ N^(1/3+ε) for Frey curves and h(E) ≪ N^(1/2+ε) for integral j are cited from [7] (arXiv 2608.23559, 24 Aug 2026), whose Theorem 1.6 I read as h(E) ≪ N^(1/2)·(log N)^4 for integral j. The 2609 paper's AI statement credits 'AI models' with suggesting the argument that gave h(E) ≪ N(log log N)^2, which the author verified and reconstructed and which motivated the stronger results; the paper does not say which model suggested it, and names OpenAI's ChatGPT-5.6 Sol Pro and ChatGPT-6 Astra and Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 and Claude Fable 5.1. 2608.23559's statement is narrower ('initial exploratory directions'). The only AI-facing review of 2609 is an AI referee (Pith, 17 Sep 2026) that asks for an expert check of its dependence on [6]; no human reading is on record. The one restricted-class proof of the statement as written, Pasten's arXiv 2308.07114 (posted 14 Aug 2023, before the freeze; CUBO 2026), proves it for E/Q whose j-invariant denominator is logarithmic in its numerator; its Corollary 1.3 gives |Δ| ≤ 256A·N^6·log N, which has the statement's form. Joshi's arXiv 2403.10430 (15 Mar 2024) claims abc and, from it, the arithmetic Szpiro inequality over number fields including Q; it is in the window, has no accepted verdict, and its only public engagement I could read is Scholze's MathOverflow comment as relayed by Woit. The IUT route to the statement (Mochizuki 2012) remains disputed, and the July 2026 LANA interim report reaches no verdict. Close calls: (i) whether 2308.07114 counts as a case of the statement or a different question: the abstract says it proves the statement, restricted to a class, and I record it that way. (ii) Whether 2609's bound moves the statement's quantity: it moves the bound on |Δ| in terms of f, but in an exponential, not polynomial, shape. (iii) Whether 2608.23559's 'initial exploratory directions' AI contribution is load-bearing for a result: the authors say it suggested directions, and do not attribute a result to a model. (iv) The 2023 versus 2026 best-bound framing is an order-of-magnitude versus constant difference, not a contradiction. Nothing in the record connects OpenAI's Astra announcement (Aug 2026) or its 722-manuscript catalogue (Oct 2026) to Szpiro or abc; the catalogue scan found no matching entry, though it was read in model-mediated chunks. The parent n-conjecture was not researched.
competing_reading: The strongest case that the problem has moved: in the window, the statement's own quantity |Δ| now has a better unconditional bound for all E/Q (N log N to N log log N, and N for semistable curves), and Frey-type partial bounds for integral j have improved; one AI-acknowledged argument produced the stronger corollaries; and the proof of the statement as written for a named class (2023, published 2026) shows it is being proved piecemeal. The opposite reading: none of these is the statement. The unconditional bounds are exponential in the conductor; the Frey-type bounds are on the Faltings height and for a stronger conjecture; the family result is subexponential; the almost-all result is statistical; the restricted-class proof predates the window; and the one route to the full statement (IUT) is disputed, with an unresolved step as of July 2026.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A character-level check of arXiv 2609.17390: the AI statement in Section 4, Theorems 1.1 to 1.3, and the imported inequality from [6] (Theorems 1.5 and 1.6 of the 2024 J. Number Theory paper), plus the Lemma 2.1 step the AI referee flags. (2) A human referee or expert report on 2609.17390, and on its journal status. (3) The full text of arXiv 2608.23559 Section 6, to see whether 'assist with computations' and 'proofread' appear and whether any computed result is load-bearing. (4) The full text of arXiv 2403.10430 (Theorem 2.10.1, Theorem 7.1.1, acknowledgements) to confirm whether the arithmetic Szpiro inequality over Q is derived, and any expert verdict on Corollary 3.12 in IUT III or Joshi's version of it, including the LANA project's final judgement and Scholze's MathOverflow comment. (5) Readable copies of Scholze and Stix (2018), Joshi's 2025 Final Report and its Nov 2025 FAQ, and the 2012 IUT papers' Corollary 3.12. (6) The Mestre–Oesterlé and Pesenti–Szpiro papers, to date them and confirm the restricted cases.
